# Randers Mave- og Tarmkirurgi

Randers Mave- og Tarmkirurgi is a gastrointestinal surgery department in Denmark that is tracked as part of national quality monitoring for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) treatment. The department's clinical performance is evaluated using standardized quality indicators maintained by DANIBD (Danish National Inflammatory Bowel Disease database).

According to the 2024 DANIBD annual report, Randers Mave- og Tarmkirurgi reported a re-operation rate of 20% for surgical procedures, which exceeds the national quality target of 8% [^src1]. Re-operation rates measure the proportion of patients requiring surgery again within 30 days of their initial surgical intervention and serve as an indicator of surgical quality and safety. A re-operation rate substantially above the development target suggests either higher surgical complexity, complications, or opportunities for quality improvement at this department.

The department's performance data is part of a broader national monitoring system that tracks both pharmacological treatment metrics—such as annual F-calprotectin measurement rates for IBD patients—and surgical quality indicators across Danish IBD treatment centers [^src1].
